title: Thermal Hall Resistivity as a Unifying Description of Phonon Thermal Hall Effect in Various Insulators
authors: Dirui Wu, Ying Kit Tsui, Xavier Loh, Minseong Lee, Eun Sang Choi, Takao Sasagawa, Toshimitsu Ito, Xiao Renshaw Wang, Pinaki Sengupta, Xinyang Zhang, Christos Panagopoulos
abstract: A considerable phonon thermal Hall effect was recently discovered across a diverse collection of materials. To clarify this enigmatic thermal Hall response in various insulators, we investigate the doped Mott insulator La$_{5/3}$Sr$_{1/3}$NiO$_4$ as an example material system and reveal a characteristic phonon-dominated thermal Hall effect. As a sensitive probe of the transverse thermal response, the thermal Hall resistivity $w_{xy}$ exhibits an insulating-like temperature dependence $w_{xy}(T)$, a linear magnetic-field dependence $w_{xy}(H)$ near $H=0$, and a $T$-linear thermal Hall angle at low temperatures. The presence of similar phenomena across a series of insulators suggests that $w_{xy}$ serves as a unifying description of phonon thermal Hall effect, corroborated by an apparent correlation between the insulating-like $w_{xy}(T)$ and material's localized electronic state.
summary: This work investigates the phonon thermal Hall effect across various insulating materials, using $	ext{La}_{5/3}	ext{Sr}_{1/3}	ext{NiO}_4$ as a primary example. By measuring the thermal Hall resistivity ($\omega_{xy}$), the authors establish that its characteristic temperature and field dependencies provide a unified description for this phenomenon in different Mott insulators.
main_problem: To establish a unifying description for the phonon thermal Hall effect (THE) observed across various insulating materials.
main_result: The thermal Hall resistivity ($\omega_{xy}$) exhibits characteristic temperature and magnetic field dependencies ($T^{-1}$ divergence, linear $H$ dependence) that serve as a unifying signature for phonon THE in diverse insulators.
method: Experimental measurements using dedicated one-heater-three-thermometer setups to measure the full thermal resistivity tensor ($\mathbf{w}$) and calculate conductivities ($ oldsymbol{\kappa}$).
model_or_system: The study focuses on doped Mott insulators, specifically $	ext{La}_{5/3}	ext{Sr}_{1/3}	ext{NiO}_4$, and compares results across other insulating systems like $	ext{SrTiO}_3$ and cuprates.
key_observables: Thermal Hall resistivity ($\omega_{xy}$), Thermal Hall angle ($	heta_{	ext{TH}}$), Longitudinal thermal conductivity ($\kappa_{xx}$), and specific heat ($C(T)$).
important_parameters: Low temperatures (down to $\sim 2$ K), magnetic fields near $H=0$, and doping levels in Mott insulators.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes an isotropic and field-antisymmetric thermal resistivity tensor ($\mathbf{w}$).
figures_summary: Figures compare measured $\kappa_{xy}$ vs. $\omega_{xy}$, showing characteristic temperature divergences ($T^{-1}, T^{-2}$) for different materials, and illustrate the linear $H$ dependence of $\omega_{xy}$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents measurements on $	ext{LSNO-1/3}$, analyzes its unique signatures ($\omega_{xy}(T)$, $\omega_{xy}(H)$), compares these findings to established data from other insulators (STO, LCO, Si), and concludes by proposing the unifying role of $\omega_{xy}$.
why_interesting: While focused on thermal transport rather than quantum dynamics, the study probes collective excitations (phonons) in strongly correlated Mott insulators, which is a key area where lattice vibrations interact with electronic correlations.

FIG. 2. Measured thermal Hall resistivity and thermal Hall angle of LSNO-1/3. (a) Temperature dependence of the anti- symmetrized thermal Hall resistance wxy at various mag- netic fields following a diverging T −1 power-law. (b) Linear magnetic-field dependence of wxy near H = 0 at different temperatures. (c) T-linear temperature dependence of the thermal Hall angle at low temperatures. These three phe- nomena can be found prevalently in other insulators showing phonon THE.
